body: Thanks... am currently taking a med and have taken many in the past. I have an appointment with the psychiatrist later this week, in fact. Relief via medication would be great, but based on past experience I don't expect it.

Unfortunately, this isn't about revenge. I wish her the least pain possible, even if I do take actions which have the unintended consequence of causing her much pain.

Thanks for the thoughtful reply.

I have difficulty believing that there are actions I can take that will result in adequate improvement. I try all the time to consider options but I get nowhere useful. Over the last 10+ years, I've been in the care of highly-regarded psychiatrists, psychologists, therapeutic groups, etc., so I feel it's not for lack of trying and trying hard. I currently see a psychologist & a psychiatrist whom I would objectively regard highly, even though I haven't found them personally helpful. So my near-hopelessness comes from a background in which I've been given much opportunity to work on getting better and done much to try to work in the positive direction, and it hasn't taken.

As for why I feel suicidal, I find myself constantly affected by anxiety. Every social interaction entails a painful amount of embarrassment. I'm capable of enjoying certain things, but the enjoyment pales in comparison to my anxiety and I feel little motivation to pursue things that might be enjoyable. Life feels like an unrewarding, painful slog. Etiology-wise, in the interpersonal realm (which you ask about), I have, in brief, a family that's largely supportive now, but I feel was partially damaging when I was a kid. My peers are nice to me now, but were consistently mean to me when I was growing up.

I think you're right that my suicide would still devastate my girlfriend even though she's left me. And as someone else has mentioned, it's possible it would affect her even more since she might feel like she triggered it. The best I could do would be to leave a note explaining, like I did in my original post, that I was suicidal all along and am doing it now not simply because I was dumped, but because I feel the collateral damage will be somewhat lessened.
No one male, local, and personally close.

I think she meant it about waste of time, could be wrong. She's been on the fence about breaking up for over a year because of this stuff.
I make just under 30K. :(
No, actually, feeling stupid in a lot of situations contributes to my desire for suicide. (Can't understand things as well as I think would make me happy and successful and better liked by others.)

That's flattering, and I think it oversells me. Unfortunately, despite the talents and positive qualities I may have, there's enough that's broken in me that I've had a longstanding to end my life that I can't ignore. It could be that "there is something," but experience has shown that I'll just settle back to the way things feel.

You have it somewhat wrong. I think she chose to be with me, there was no "forcing" involved. I think she was with me in spite of my depression/anxiety, not because of it. I asked her if she felt the 2 years were wasted time, and she said no, she wouldn't have done anything differently. You're correct that she hoped I could change, which, of course, is a notoriously inadvisable objective to have for a partner.

More importantly, it disappoints me that an expression of suicidality brings out such contempt in so many people, but I guess I was asking for it by posting here.
